text:
Soup curry or miso ramen for your first night in Sapporo? We'd say both, just not at the same time: soup curry for dinner, then ramen around 1 a.m. That's how Susukino ends its nights 👇

🤔 A or B: soup curry in a basement downtown, or out in a residential neighbourhood? Pick one, then see where we'd go 👉 https://japanbystation.com/sapporo-where-locals-eat

🅰️ SOUP CURRY DOWNTOWN

Garaku sits in a basement near Odori. The pork-bone and herb broth simmers for two days, with kelp and bonito added, and the shop closes when it runs out. Go early.

🅱️ SOUP CURRY WHERE PEOPLE LIVE

Kotoni is a few stops west on JR or the Tozai Line. Picante cooks each curry in its own small pot under the JR station, and Sapporo Rakkyo nearby is a gentle first try (closed the third Wednesday of the month).

🍜 AND THE LATE BOWL

Ganso Ramen Yokocho is a 42-metre alley of 17 miso ramen shops, crowded from morning to night. Keyaki, three minutes from Susukino Station, is open 10:00 to 2:00, every day of the year.

💡 HOW TO ORDER SOUP CURRY

Pick the spice level, the rice size and one or two toppings. Two is plenty, because the bowl already has big pieces of Hokkaido vegetables.

👉 Plus a free shuttle to a seafood breakfast and a bath inside the market:
https://japanbystation.com/sapporo-where-locals-eat
